# AccessScan

> Free, local-first WCAG/EAA accessibility scanner. Checks any public website
> for accessibility issues using axe-core via headless Chromium. No accounts,
> no payments, no database, no cloud — results stay on your machine.

## What it does

- Paste a URL (bare domains like `example.com` work) → scans the page with
  axe-core WCAG 2.x A/AA rules
- Optional crawl mode: scans up to 10 same-origin pages (concurrency 2)
- Reports violations by severity (critical/serious/moderate/minor), WCAG
  criteria, fix guidance, and "needs manual review" items axe couldn't decide
- Exports self-contained HTML report, JSON, or PDF
- Compares scans of the same URL: shows added/fixed rules vs. previous scan
- Bundled plain-English reference for 91 axe rules at /rules.html
- SSRF-hardened: blocks private/internal hosts, re-validates redirect targets,
  strips URL credentials before storing

## Honest limits

- Automated scanners catch roughly 30–57% of WCAG issues — a clean scan is
  not a compliance guarantee. Manual audit still required for EAA.
- Results are in-memory only; export reports before restarting.
- Local tool: binds 127.0.0.1, single scan at a time, rate-limited.

## Links

- Live: https://access-scan-tool.vercel.app
- Repo: https://github.com/Afkhomie/AccessScan
- Rules reference: /rules.html
- Security model: /security.html — how scans are kept local and targets are hardened
- Reliability & limits: /reliability.html — what the scanner can and can't detect
- License: MIT

## For agents

- API: POST /api/scan {url, crawl?, maxPages?} → 202 {id}; poll
  GET /api/scan/:id; GET /api/scans/:id/compare;
  GET /api/scan/:id/export?format=html|json|pdf
- Run: `npm install && node server.js` → http://localhost:3000
- Tests: `node test/smoke.js && node test/smoke2.js`
